chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Presenting gospel groups in Texas in 1954
summary: He recalls promoting the Five Blind Boys, Soul Stirrers and Pilgrim Travelers in four Texas towns.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: And, let's see. You had Butterbeans and Suzy, you had Pearl Bailey's show and you had...oh, and incidentally, during this period, all along this period, you had singing groups that were becoming famous. I know in Dallas, in '54 I had... I presented The Five Blind Boys, The Soul Stirrers and The Pilgrim Travelers. I was one of the first to present Sam Cooke with a group. And, again, all of these people came in Dallas. I thought there was another automobile wreck.

You know, when you are a promoter, or you are the recipient of something good, it's a strange feeling. Sometimes you ask yourself, "What did I do to deserve this?" Here are three thousand people coming, walking, running, in cabs and buses, coming out to hear these singing groups...The Five Blind Boys, The Pilgrim Travelers and The Soul Stirrers. And I had them...I played them in four concerts--Denison, Greenville, Dallas and Paris, Texas. Very, very successful. So it's that funny feeling that you get, Dan, during...you promote something that you believe in and that you find out that other people...you convince them, too.
